answer: In a peer to peer agent economy, capital lockup resists sybils because each new identity must stake a bond that also throttles its gossip rate, so flooding the network topology with fake peers costs linearly per node. An attacker spawning a thousand identities locks a thousand bonds, while each node still forwards only validated ripple updates to its neighbors, so latency and bandwidth overheads scale with the sybil count, not against honest peers.
